items.followUp: What is the least count of a standard Vernier Callipers, and what is it used to measure?

rubric.why: Award for describing the instrument and its use.
rubric.description: Defines Vernier Callipers as an instrument for measuring small lengths or dimensions accurately.
rubric.how: Look for the instrument’s purpose and an example of a dimension it measures.

rubric.why: Award for the least count of Digital Vernier Callipers.
rubric.description: States the least count as 0.01 mm (equivalent to 0.001 cm).
rubric.how: Accept either equivalent value with its unit.

modelAnswer: Vernier Callipers are an instrument used to measure small lengths, such as the internal or external diameter and depth of an object, accurately.
The least count of Digital Vernier Callipers is 0.01 mm (0.001 cm).

items.followUp: State four rules for identifying significant figures in a measured value.

rubric.why: These rules identify significant nonzero digits and captive zeros.
rubric.description: States that all nonzero digits and zeros between nonzero digits are significant.
rubric.how: Look for both nonzero digits and zeros between nonzero digits being counted.

rubric.why: These rules distinguish leading zeros from trailing decimal zeros.
rubric.description: States that leading zeros are not significant, while zeros at the end of a decimal number are significant.
rubric.how: Look for the correct treatment of both kinds of zeros.

modelAnswer: All non-zero digits are significant.
Zeros between non-zero digits are significant.
Zeros to the left of the first non-zero digit are not significant.
Zeros at the end of a number to the right of the decimal point are significant.

items.followUp: Write the three equations of motion for an object falling freely from rest, taking downward as positive.

rubric.why: This is the first equation of motion with acceleration due to gravity.
rubric.description: Writes the first equation of motion for motion under gravity.

rubric.why: The other two standard equations complete the set.
rubric.description: Writes the displacement-time and velocity-displacement equations for motion under gravity.
rubric.how: Check for h (or s) = ut + ½gt² and v² = u² + 2gh (or 2gs).

modelAnswer: Taking downward as positive, the acceleration is g.
v = u + gt
h = ut + ½gt²
v² = u² + 2gh

items.followUp: Define limiting friction and write the relation between coefficient of friction and normal reaction.

rubric.why: Limiting friction is the maximum friction immediately before sliding begins.
rubric.how: Look for maximum friction and the onset of motion or sliding.

rubric.why: The coefficient is the ratio of limiting friction to normal reaction.
rubric.description: Defines coefficient of friction and gives its relation to the forces.
rubric.how: Check for the ratio μ = Fs/Fn, or an equivalent verbal definition.

modelAnswer: Force of limiting friction (Fs) is the maximum frictional force that acts between two surfaces just before one surface starts sliding over the other.
The coefficient of friction (μ) is the ratio of limiting friction to the normal reaction: μ = Fs/Fn.

items.followUp: Give two useful effects and two harmful effects of friction.

rubric.why: These are examples of useful effects of friction.
rubric.description: Gives two advantages of friction, such as enabling walking, writing, grip or braking.
rubric.how: Award for two distinct valid advantages.

rubric.why: These are common harmful effects of friction.
rubric.description: Gives two disadvantages, such as wear and tear, heat production or energy loss.
rubric.how: Award for two distinct valid disadvantages.

modelAnswer: Advantages: Friction enables us to walk without slipping and allows brakes to stop vehicles.
Disadvantages: Friction causes wear and tear of moving parts and produces unwanted heat, wasting energy.

items.followUp: Define inertia and write the formula for momentum.

rubric.why: Inertia is an object's resistance to a change in its state of rest or motion.
rubric.description: Defines inertia as resistance to a change in the state of rest or motion.
rubric.how: Look for resistance to a change in rest or motion.

rubric.why: Momentum is the product of mass and velocity.
rubric.description: Defines momentum and gives its mathematical relation.
rubric.how: Check for momentum = mass × velocity or p = mv.

modelAnswer: Inertia is the property of a body by which it resists any change in its state of rest or uniform motion.
Momentum is the product of a body's mass and velocity: p = mv.

items.followUp: Define acceleration and explain what is meant by uniform acceleration.

rubric.why: Acceleration measures how quickly velocity changes with time.
rubric.description: Defines acceleration as the rate of change of velocity with time.
rubric.how: Look for change in velocity per unit time.

rubric.why: This is the defining condition for uniform acceleration.
rubric.description: Defines uniform acceleration using equal velocity changes in equal time intervals.
rubric.how: Check that both equal changes in velocity and equal time intervals are stated.

modelAnswer: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with time.
Uniform acceleration occurs when a body undergoes equal changes in velocity in equal intervals of time.

items.followUp: A force of 10 N acts perpendicularly at a distance of 0.4 m from a pivot. Calculate its torque.

rubric.why: Torque describes the turning effect of a force about a pivot or axis.
rubric.description: Defines torque as the turning effect of a force about a pivot or axis of rotation.
rubric.how: Look for the turning effect of force and its reference point or axis.

rubric.why: Torque equals force multiplied by the perpendicular distance from the pivot.
rubric.description: Gives the mathematical equation for torque, with its unit.
rubric.how: Check for force × perpendicular distance and accept N m as the unit.

modelAnswer: Torque is the turning effect of a force about a pivot or axis of rotation.
Torque = Force × perpendicular distance from the pivot: τ = F × d.
The SI unit of torque is newton metre (N m).
